events.quote: In 1895 Jock Willis sold Cutty Sark to the Portuguese firm Joaquim Antunes Ferreira for £1,250 . She was renamed Ferreira after the firm

events.text: She was dismasted off the Cape of Good Hope.

events.quote: In May 1916 she was dismasted off the Cape of Good Hope

events.text: She was re-rigged over 18 months to a barquentine sail arrangement.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In May 1916 she was dismasted off the Cape of Good Hope because of the rolling of the ship in bad weather and had to be towed into Table Bay off Cape Town . Because of World War I , it was impossible to obtain suitable materials to replace the masts so she was re-rigged over 18 months to a barquentine sail arrangement

events.text: Ferreira was the last clipper operating anywhere in the world.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1922 Ferreira was the last clipper operating anywhere in the world

events.text: The ship returned to Lisbon, where she was sold to new owners and renamed Maria do Amparo.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1922 Ferreira was the last clipper operating anywhere in the world . Caught in a storm in the English Channel she put into Falmouth harbour where she was spotted by retired merchant navy captain Wilfred Dowman of Flushing , Cornwall , who was then operating the training ship Lady of Avenel . The ship returned to Lisbon , where she was sold to new owners and renamed Maria do Amparo

events.text: She was used as committee boat for the regatta week in Fowey.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1924 she was used as committee boat for the regatta week in Fowey

events.text: The ship was given by Catharine Dowman to the Incorporated Thames Nautical Training College, HMS Worcester at Greenhithe.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Dowman died in 1936 and the ship was given by Catharine Dowman , his widow , along with £5000 for maintenance , to the Incorporated Thames Nautical Training College , HMS Worcester at Greenhithe

events.text: By 1950 she had become surplus to requirements.
